newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wiluna says gold output up and costs down.
newsitem.headline: Wiluna says gold output up and costs down.

text.p: Wiluna Mines Ltd said on Tuesday it knocked down operating costs and sold more gold in the second quarter ended June 30 than in the March quarter.
The average cash operating cost on 29,289 ounces of gold sold in the June quarter was A$426 an ounce, the company said.
This compares with 24,002 ounces mined at an average cash cost of A$524 an ounce in the March quarter, Wiluna said.
A hedging programme allowed the company to realise an average price of A$606 an ounce in the June quarter compared with a spot market price of A$446 an ounce, the company said.

A higer production rate and improved ore grades mined from Wiluna's Bulletin lode in Western Australia were the main factors behind the reduction in costs, Wiluna managing director Jeff Gresham said in a statement.
Improved performance of a gold processing plant led to a further reduction of cash operating costs to an average of A$327 an ounce for the month of June, Gresham said.
Operating costs should fall a further A$27 an ounce once a new power station due to start up in October is fully operational, Gresham said.
The recent fall in the international gold price to 12-year lows has place added focus on cash operating costs and hedging portfolios among Australian gold miners.
On average, it cost A$460 an ounce to mine gold in Australia in 1996, figures fronm the Perth Mint show.
Wiluna said it increased its hedging during the June quarter by 72,000 ounces. As of June 30, it had forward sold 312,850 ounces at an average price of A$564 an ounce, it said.
For 1998, some 102,000 ounces are forward sold at an average price of A$551 an ounce, the company said.
Gold currently fetches about A$434 an ounce.
